cards.front: I enjoy playing pickleball with my coworkers after work.
cards.back: 我喜歡下班後和同事一起打匹克球。
cards.note: enjoy / avoid / finish / mind / suggest / keep + V-ing：這些動詞後面接動名詞，不接 to V。

cards.front: She suggested taking the train instead of renting a car.
cards.back: 她建議搭火車，不要租車。
cards.note: suggest + V-ing（也可以說 suggest that we take…）；不能說 suggest to take。

cards.front: We finished checking in and went straight to the gate.
cards.back: 我們辦好登機手續，就直接去登機門。
cards.note: finish + V-ing：完成某件事。

cards.front: We decided to book the hotel near the stadium.
cards.back: 我們決定訂球場附近的飯店。
cards.note: decide / plan / hope / want / need + to V：這些動詞後面接 to + 原形。

cards.front: I can't afford to miss the first pitch.
cards.note: afford / manage / refuse / promise + to V。

cards.front: I'm not used to waking up this early for a flight.
cards.back: 我不習慣為了搭飛機這麼早起。
cards.note: be used to + V-ing：習慣於（to 是介系詞，後面接名詞或 V-ing）。

cards.front: I used to watch every baseball game, but now I only watch the playoffs.
cards.back: 我以前每場棒球賽都看，現在只看季後賽。
cards.note: used to + 原形動詞：過去的習慣（現在已經沒有了）。跟 be used to + V-ing 意思不同。

cards.front: I forgot to bring my passport, so I had to go back home.
cards.back: 我忘了帶護照，所以必須回家。
cards.note: forget + to V：忘了去做（那件事還沒做）。

cards.front: I will never forget visiting Kyoto for the first time.
cards.back: 我永遠不會忘記第一次去京都。
cards.note: forget / remember + V-ing：忘記／記得「已經做過的事」。跟 forget to V 意思不同。

cards.front: He stopped to buy a bottle of water on the way to the court.
cards.back: 他在去球場的路上停下來買了一瓶水。
cards.note: stop + to V：停下來，去做另一件事。

cards.front: Please stop talking during the presentation.
cards.note: stop + V-ing：停止正在做的事。

cards.front: I'm interested in learning Japanese for my next trip.
cards.back: 我有興趣為下次旅行學日文。
cards.note: 介系詞後面接 V-ing：interested in / good at / afraid of / thank you for。

cards.front: I'm looking forward to seeing you at the meeting.
cards.back: 我期待在會議上見到你。
cards.note: look forward to + V-ing：這裡的 to 是介系詞，所以後面接 V-ing，不是原形。

cards.front: It is difficult to find a good seat on opening day.
cards.back: 開幕日很難找到好位子。
cards.note: It is + 形容詞 + to V：用來說明某件事的難易、好壞。

cards.front: She taught me how to serve in pickleball.
cards.note: 疑問詞 + to V：how to / where to / what to / when to。

cards.front: Do you know what time the museum opens?
cards.back: 你知道博物館幾點開門嗎？
cards.note: Do you know + 疑問詞 + 主詞 + 動詞：不再用助動詞 does，動詞也不倒裝。

cards.front: Excuse me, could you tell me how I can get to the station?
cards.back: 不好意思，可以告訴我怎麼去車站嗎？
cards.note: how + 主詞 + can（不是 how can I）：助動詞放在主詞後面。

cards.front: I'd like to know whether the flight is on time.
cards.back: 我想知道班機是否準時。
cards.note: 沒有疑問詞時，用 whether 或 if 帶出間接問句。

cards.front: Can you tell me if this bus goes to the airport?
cards.back: 可以告訴我這班公車有到機場嗎？
cards.note: 是非問句改成間接問句：if / whether + 肯定句語序（不是 does this bus go）。

cards.front: She asked me where I was going.
cards.note: 轉述問句：語序用肯定句（where I was going），不是 where was I going。

cards.front: I have no idea who will be at the meeting.
cards.back: 我不知道誰會參加會議。
cards.note: 疑問詞當主詞時語序本來就不變：who will be。

cards.front: Could you explain why the schedule changed?
cards.back: 可以解釋為什麼行程改了嗎？
cards.note: why + 主詞 + 動詞（changed）：不要再加 did。

cards.front: Let me know when the game starts.
cards.back: 比賽幾點開始請告訴我。
cards.note: Let me know 後面接的也是間接問句：when + 主詞 + 動詞。

cards.front: I'm not sure how much the room costs per night.
cards.back: 我不確定房間一晚多少錢。
cards.note: how much + 主詞 + 動詞（costs）：肯定句語序。

cards.front: Do you remember where we parked the car?
cards.back: 你記得我們把車停在哪裡嗎？
cards.note: 正確：where we parked；錯誤：where did we park。

cards.front: I have worked at this company for three years.
cards.back: 我在這家公司工作三年了。
cards.note: for + 一段時間：現在完成式表示「從過去一直持續到現在」。

cards.front: She has lived in Taipei since 2019.
cards.back: 她從二〇一九年起就住在台北。
cards.note: since + 起點時間（2019、Monday、last year）。

cards.front: Have you ever been to Japan?
cards.note: ever：問「有沒有這個經驗」。have been to = 去過（已經回來了）。

cards.front: I have never tried pickleball before.
cards.back: 我以前從沒試過匹克球。
cards.note: never + 現在完成式：到現在為止從來沒有。

cards.front: We have already booked the hotel.
cards.note: already：已經（放在 have 和過去分詞中間）。
not ... yet：還沒（通常放句尾）。
有明確的過去時間（yesterday、last week、in 2020）要用過去式，不能用現在完成式。

cards.front: I have lost my wallet, so I can't pay for lunch.
cards.back: 我的錢包不見了，所以沒辦法付午餐錢。
cards.note: 強調過去的事「對現在的影響」時用現在完成式。

cards.front: How long have you been waiting for the bus?
cards.note: How long + have + 主詞 + been + V-ing：問動作持續了多久。

cards.front: I have been learning English for two years, and I'm still improving.
cards.back: 我學英文兩年了，而且還在進步。
cards.note: have been V-ing（現在完成進行式）：強調動作從過去持續到現在。

cards.front: Last month I almost missed my train to Kaohsiung. I woke up late, so I took a taxi to the station. The traffic was terrible, and I arrived five minutes before the departure time. I ran to the platform and jumped on just as the doors were closing. I was out of breath, but I was happy to be on board. Next time, I will set two alarms.
cards.back: 上個月我差點錯過去高雄的火車。我睡過頭，所以搭計程車去車站。路上塞車很嚴重，我在發車前五分鐘才到。我跑到月台，在車門正要關上時跳上車。我氣喘吁吁，但很高興趕上了。下次我會設兩個鬧鐘。
cards.note: 重點：almost 差點／departure 出發／out of breath 上氣不接下氣

questions.q: How did the writer get to the station?
questions.explain: 文中：I took a taxi to the station（我搭計程車去車站）。

questions.q: When did the writer get on the train?
questions.explain: 文中：jumped on just as the doors were closing（車門正要關上時跳上車）。

questions.q: What will the writer do next time?
questions.explain: 最後一句：Next time, I will set two alarms（下次設兩個鬧鐘）。

cards.front: When we arrived at the hotel, the receptionist asked for our names and passports. She said our room was not ready yet, but we could leave our luggage at the front desk. She also gave us a map and explained how to get to the night market. After a short walk, we came back, and our room was ready. It had a great view of the city.
cards.back: 我們抵達飯店時，櫃檯人員請我們出示姓名和護照。她說房間還沒準備好，但我們可以把行李寄放在櫃檯。她還給了我們一張地圖，並說明怎麼去夜市。走了一小段路回來後，房間已經準備好了，窗外的城市景色很棒。
cards.note: 重點：receptionist 櫃檯接待／front desk 櫃檯／view 景色

questions.q: Why couldn't the guests go to their room right away?
questions.explain: 文中：our room was not ready yet（房間還沒準備好）。

questions.q: What did the receptionist give them?
options: A key to the night market
questions.explain: 文中：She also gave us a map（她還給了我們一張地圖）。

questions.q: What was good about the room?
questions.explain: 最後一句：It had a great view of the city（可以看到很棒的城市景色）。

cards.front: I was looking for the museum, but I got lost. I asked a woman on the street, "Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the museum?" She smiled and said it was a ten-minute walk. "Go straight, turn left at the bank, and you will see it on your right." I thanked her and followed her directions. It was easy to find.
cards.back: 我在找博物館，但是迷路了。我問路上的一位女士：「不好意思，可以告訴我怎麼去博物館嗎？」她微笑著說走路大約十分鐘。「直走，在銀行那裡左轉，就會在右手邊看到。」我謝謝她，照著她說的走，很容易就找到了。
cards.note: 重點：get lost 迷路／could you tell me how to… 間接問句／on your right 在你右手邊

questions.q: Why did the writer ask a woman for help?
questions.explain: 文中：I got lost（我迷路了），所以才問路。

questions.q: How far was the museum?
questions.explain: 文中：it was a ten-minute walk（走路十分鐘）。

questions.q: Where is the museum, according to the woman?
options: On the right, after turning left at the bank
On the left, before the bank
questions.explain: 文中：turn left at the bank, and you will see it on your right（在銀行左轉，博物館在你的右邊）。

cards.front: Last Friday I arrived at the airport two hours before my flight. I checked in at the counter and dropped off my big suitcase. The staff member said my carry-on bag was too heavy, so I moved a book into my backpack. Then I showed my boarding pass at security and walked to gate 12. Because I was early, I had time to buy a coffee and relax.
cards.back: 上週五我在班機起飛前兩小時到了機場。我在櫃檯辦好登機手續，託運了大行李箱。地勤人員說我的隨身行李太重，所以我把一本書放進背包。接著我在安檢出示登機證，走向十二號登機門。因為我很早到，還有時間買杯咖啡休息一下。
cards.note: 重點：check in 辦理登機／carry-on 隨身行李／boarding pass 登機證

questions.q: How early did the writer arrive at the airport?
questions.explain: 文中：two hours before my flight（起飛前兩小時）。

questions.q: What did the writer do because the carry-on bag was too heavy?
options: Moved a book into the backpack
questions.explain: 文中：I moved a book into my backpack（把一本書放進背包）。

questions.q: What does "relax" mean in the last sentence?
questions.explain: relax 是放鬆、休息。因為很早到，所以有時間買咖啡放鬆。

cards.front: On my way to Seattle, I had a six-hour layover in Dubai. The airport was crowded, but I found a quiet seat near a window. I ate dinner, walked around the shops, and called my family. At night, an announcement said that my next flight had a short delay. I was tired, but I was glad to have enough time to rest.
cards.back: 前往西雅圖的路上，我在杜拜有六小時的中途停留。機場很擁擠，但我在窗邊找到一個安靜的位子。我吃了晚餐、逛了逛店，還打電話給家人。晚上廣播說我的下一班飛機會稍微延誤。我很累，但很高興有足夠的時間休息。
cards.note: 重點：layover 中途停留／crowded 擁擠的／delay 延誤

questions.q: How long was the layover?
questions.explain: 文中：a six-hour layover（六小時的中途停留）。

questions.q: Where did the writer sit?
questions.explain: 文中：a quiet seat near a window（窗邊安靜的位子）。

questions.q: What did the announcement say?
options: The next flight had a short delay
questions.explain: 文中：my next flight had a short delay（下一班飛機稍微延誤）。

cards.front: On the last morning of our trip, we packed our bags and went to the front desk to check out. The receptionist asked if we had used anything from the minibar. We said no, and she returned our deposit of fifty dollars. She also sent us a receipt by email. Before leaving, I thanked the housekeeping staff for the clean room.
cards.back: 旅行的最後一天早上，我們收好行李，到櫃檯退房。接待人員問我們有沒有用過小冰箱裡的東西。我們說沒有，她就退還了五十美元的押金。她也用電子郵件寄給我們收據。離開前，我謝謝客房清潔人員把房間整理得很乾淨。
cards.note: 重點：check out 退房／deposit 押金／receipt 收據

questions.q: What did the receptionist ask?
options: If they used anything from the minibar
questions.explain: 文中：asked if we had used anything from the minibar（問有沒有用小冰箱的東西）。

questions.q: How much deposit was returned?
questions.explain: 文中：our deposit of fifty dollars（五十美元的押金）。

questions.q: How did the writer get the receipt?
questions.explain: 文中：She also sent us a receipt by email（用電子郵件寄收據）。

cards.front: To go to the old town, we had to transfer trains at the central station. I checked the timetable on my phone and found the right platform. The fare was only three dollars, and the next train came in five minutes. It was crowded, so we stood near the door. Fifteen minutes later, we arrived and walked to the market.
cards.back: 要去老城區，我們得在中央車站轉車。我用手機查了時刻表，找到正確的月台。車資只要三美元，下一班車五分鐘後就來了。車上很擠，所以我們站在門邊。十五分鐘後我們到了，然後走去市場。
cards.note: 重點：transfer 轉乘／timetable 時刻表／fare 車資

questions.q: Where did they change trains?
questions.explain: 文中：transfer trains at the central station（在中央車站轉車）。

questions.q: How much was the fare?
questions.explain: 文中：The fare was only three dollars（車資只要三美元）。

questions.q: Why did they stand near the door?
questions.explain: 文中：It was crowded, so we stood near the door（很擠，所以站在門邊）。

cards.front: My friend is a vegetarian, and I am allergic to shrimp, so choosing a restaurant is not always easy. Last night, we told the waiter about our needs before ordering. He recommended a vegetable appetizer and a chicken soup for me. The food was delicious, and the service was great. When we asked for the bill, we left a ten percent tip.
cards.back: 我的朋友吃素，而我對蝦子過敏，所以選餐廳不一定容易。昨天晚上，我們點餐前先告訴服務生我們的需求。他為朋友推薦了蔬菜開胃菜，也為我推薦了一份雞肉湯。食物很美味，服務也很棒。我們要求結帳時，留了百分之十的小費。
cards.note: 重點：vegetarian 素食者／allergic 過敏的／tip 小費

questions.q: What is the writer allergic to?
questions.explain: 文中：I am allergic to shrimp（我對蝦子過敏）。

questions.q: When did they tell the waiter about their needs?
questions.explain: 文中：told the waiter about our needs before ordering（點餐前先告訴服務生）。

questions.q: How much tip did they leave?
questions.explain: 最後一句：a ten percent tip（百分之十的小費）。

cards.front: On the second day of our trip, I woke up with a bad stomachache. My sister helped me walk to a pharmacy near the hotel. The pharmacist asked a few questions and gave me some medicine. I felt much better in the evening. This experience taught me to bring basic medicine and to learn how to ask for help in an emergency.
cards.back: 旅行的第二天，我醒來時肚子很痛。姊姊陪我走到飯店附近的藥局。藥師問了幾個問題，給了我一些藥。到了晚上我好多了。這次經驗讓我學到要帶基本的藥品，也要學會在緊急情況下怎麼求助。
cards.note: 重點：pharmacy 藥局／emergency 緊急情況／how to 怎麼做（疑問詞 + to V）

questions.q: What happened on the second day of the trip?
questions.explain: 文中：I woke up with a bad stomachache（醒來肚子很痛）。

questions.q: Who helped the writer walk to the pharmacy?
questions.explain: 文中：My sister helped me walk to a pharmacy（姊姊陪我走到藥局）。

questions.q: What did the writer learn from this experience?
questions.explain: 最後一句：taught me to bring basic medicine（學到要帶基本的藥品）。

cards.front: We joined a guided tour of the old castle on Sunday morning. The admission was cheaper with a student discount, and the guide spoke slowly, so I understood most of the story. The castle was a famous landmark, so it was very crowded. At the end of the tour, I bought a small souvenir for my mother. It was a great way to learn about the city.
cards.back: 星期天早上，我們參加了老城堡的導覽行程。用學生折扣，入場費比較便宜，而且導覽員說得很慢，所以我聽懂了大部分的故事。這座城堡是有名的地標，所以非常擁擠。導覽結束時，我為媽媽買了一個小紀念品。這是認識這座城市很棒的方式。
cards.note: 重點：guided tour 導覽行程／admission 入場費／landmark 地標

questions.q: Why was the admission cheaper?
options: The writer had a student discount
questions.explain: 文中：cheaper with a student discount（用學生折扣比較便宜）。

questions.q: Why did the writer understand most of the story?
options: The writer read a book first
questions.explain: 文中：the guide spoke slowly（導覽員說得很慢）。

questions.q: What does "landmark" mean here?
options: A famous place that people recognize
questions.explain: landmark 是地標，知名、容易辨認的地方。

cards.front: If it rains tomorrow, the game will be canceled.
cards.back: 如果明天下雨，比賽會取消。
cards.note: 第一類條件句（可能發生）：if + 現在式，will + 原形。if 子句不用 will。

cards.front: If you heat water to 100 degrees, it boils.
cards.back: 水加熱到一百度就會沸騰。
cards.note: 零類條件句（事實或通則）：if + 現在式，現在式。

cards.front: I will call you if I arrive late.
cards.back: 如果我會晚到，我會打給你。
cards.note: if 子句放在後面時，中間不用逗號。

cards.front: If we leave now, we won't miss the train.
cards.back: 如果現在出發，我們不會錯過火車。
cards.note: 主要子句用 will 的否定：won't + 原形。

cards.front: Unless you hurry, you will miss the flight.
cards.back: 除非你快一點，否則會趕不上班機。
cards.note: unless = if ... not：後面不用再加 not。

cards.front: If I were you, I would book the tickets today.
cards.back: 如果我是你，我今天就會訂票。
cards.note: 第二類條件句（與現在事實相反）：if + 過去式，would + 原形；be 動詞一律用 were。

cards.front: If I won the lottery, I would travel around the world.
cards.back: 如果我中樂透，我就會環遊世界。
cards.note: 第二類條件句：不可能或不太可能的假設。

cards.front: What would you do if you lost your passport abroad?
cards.back: 如果你在國外弄丟護照，你會怎麼辦？
cards.note: 疑問句也可以用第二類條件句：What would you do if + 過去式？

cards.front: If you need any help, just let me know.
cards.back: 如果需要幫忙，告訴我就好。
cards.note: if + 現在式，後面也可以接祈使句（請求、建議）。

cards.front: She would take the job if the salary were higher.
cards.back: 如果薪水再高一點，她就會接這份工作。
cards.note: 第二類條件句：主詞是 she 也用 were（if the salary were higher）。

cards.front: You should check the weather before you pack.
cards.back: 打包前你應該先看一下天氣。
cards.note: should：建議、應該。

cards.front: You must show your passport at the border.
cards.back: 你在邊境必須出示護照。
cards.note: must：規定或強烈的必要性。

cards.front: You don't have to wear a suit to the interview.
cards.note: don't have to：不需要（沒有義務），不是「不可以」。

cards.front: You mustn't use your phone during the exam.
cards.note: mustn't：禁止。跟 don't have to 完全不同。

cards.front: The train might be late because of the storm.
cards.back: 因為暴風雨，火車可能會誤點。
cards.note: might：有可能（把握不高）。

cards.front: We could take a taxi if the bus is full.
cards.back: 如果公車客滿，我們可以搭計程車。
cards.note: could：提出可行的選項。

cards.front: You should have called me when the flight was canceled.
cards.back: 班機取消時你應該打給我的。
cards.note: should have + 過去分詞：當時該做卻沒做（有點責備或遺憾）。

cards.front: He must have forgotten the meeting, because he isn't here.
cards.back: 他一定是忘了開會，因為他不在這裡。
cards.note: must have + 過去分詞：對過去的事做肯定的推測。

stages.title: 單字・體育（棒球、匹克球）

cards.note: The pitcher threw a perfect game.
The score was tied after eight innings.
He ended the game with a strikeout.
She hit a home run in the ninth inning.
The manager called the bullpen.
Our lineup is strong this season.
Our team made the playoffs for the first time.
I bought a new paddle for pickleball.
You must serve underhand in pickleball.
We had a long rally before she scored.
A soft dink over the net won the point.
Try to volley the ball before it bounces.
The batter hit the first pitch over the fence.
The catcher gave a signal to the pitcher.
She caught the ball deep in the outfield.
The shortstop made a great throw to first base.
The umpire said the runner was out.
A foul ball flew into the crowd.
His fastball is over 150 kilometers per hour.
He tried to bunt the ball to move the runner.
The runner tried to steal second base.
The shortstop started a double play to end the inning.

cards.back: （匹克球）廚房區；網前不可截擊區
cards.note: You can't volley the ball when you stand in the kitchen.
Stepping on the line while you serve is a fault.
There are four pickleball courts near my house.
Her serve landed just inside the baseline.
The ball landed out of bounds, so we lost the point.
I like playing doubles with my friends.
Our opponents were very good at the net.
We always warm up for ten minutes before we play.

cards.front: My friends and I went to a baseball game on Saturday night. We bought hot dogs and cold drinks and found our seats behind first base. In the seventh inning, everyone stood up and sang a song together. In the ninth inning, our team hit a home run and won the game. The whole stadium was shouting with joy.
cards.back: 星期六晚上，我和朋友去看了一場棒球賽。我們買了熱狗和冷飲，找到一壘後方的座位。第七局時，所有人站起來一起唱歌。第九局，我們的球隊打出全壘打並贏下比賽。整個球場都在歡呼。
cards.note: 重點：seats 座位／inning 局／home run 全壘打

questions.q: Where were their seats?
questions.explain: 文中：found our seats behind first base（座位在一壘後方）。

questions.q: What happened in the seventh inning?
options: Everyone stood up and sang a song
The game was stopped by rain
questions.explain: 文中：In the seventh inning, everyone stood up and sang a song together（第七局大家站起來一起唱歌）。

questions.q: How did the game end?
options: The team won after a home run
questions.explain: 文中：In the ninth inning, our team hit a home run and won the game（第九局打出全壘打並獲勝）。

cards.front: Pickleball is easy to learn, which is why so many people enjoy it. The court is smaller than a tennis court, and the ball moves more slowly. You must let the ball bounce once on each side before you volley. Beginners usually spend their first few games trying to serve the ball over the net. After a week, most people can keep a rally going.
cards.back: 匹克球很容易學，所以很多人喜歡。球場比網球場小，球速也比較慢。球在兩邊各要落地一次，才可以截擊。初學者通常在最初幾場比賽都在努力把球發過網。一週後，大多數人都能持續對打。
cards.note: 重點：bounce 彈跳／volley 截擊／rally 來回對打

questions.q: Why do many people enjoy pickleball?
questions.explain: 第一句：Pickleball is easy to learn, which is why so many people enjoy it。

questions.q: How is a pickleball court different from a tennis court?
questions.explain: 文中：The court is smaller than a tennis court（比網球場小）。

questions.q: What do beginners spend their first games doing?
options: Trying to serve the ball over the net
questions.explain: 文中：trying to serve the ball over the net（試著把球發過網）。

cards.front: In October, baseball fans around the world watch the playoffs. Every game matters because one loss can end a team's season. Starting pitchers work hard to keep the other team from scoring, and the bullpen takes over when they get tired. A single strikeout in the last inning can change everything. Fans stay glued to their screens until the final out.
cards.back: 十月，世界各地的棒球迷都在看季後賽。每一場比賽都很重要，因為輸一場就可能結束整季。先發投手努力不讓對手得分，累了之後由牛棚接手。最後一局的一次三振就可能改變一切。球迷們盯著螢幕，直到最後一個出局數。
cards.note: 重點：playoffs 季後賽／pitcher 投手／strikeout 三振

questions.q: Why does every playoff game matter?
options: One loss can end a team's season
questions.explain: 文中：one loss can end a team's season（輸一場就可能結束整季）。

questions.q: What does the bullpen do?
options: Takes over when starting pitchers get tired
questions.explain: 文中：the bullpen takes over when they get tired（先發投手累了由牛棚接手）。

questions.q: What does "glued to their screens" mean?
questions.explain: glued to 是「黏在上面」，形容目不轉睛地看。

cards.front: A baseball game has nine innings. In each inning, both teams get a turn to bat. The pitcher throws the ball, and the batter tries to hit it. If the batter gets three strikes, the batter is out. If a player hits the ball and runs around all four bases, the team scores a run. The team with more runs at the end of the game wins.
cards.back: 一場棒球賽有九局。每一局，兩隊都有輪流打擊的機會。投手投球，打者試著把球打出去。如果打者被三次好球，就出局了。如果球員把球打出去並跑完四個壘包，球隊就得一分。比賽結束時得分較多的隊伍獲勝。
cards.note: 重點：inning 局／batter 打者／strike 好球／score a run 得分

questions.q: How many innings are in a baseball game?
questions.explain: 第一句：A baseball game has nine innings。

questions.q: When is a batter out?
questions.explain: 文中：If the batter gets three strikes, the batter is out（三次好球就出局）。

questions.q: How does a team score a run?
options: A player hits the ball and runs around all four bases
A pitcher strikes out three players
questions.explain: 文中：hits the ball and runs around all four bases, the team scores a run（打出去並跑完四個壘包就得一分）。

cards.front: Last weekend, my coworker Ken invited me to watch a baseball game. Our seats were near the outfield, so we could see the players clearly. In the third inning, a foul ball flew toward us, and everyone jumped up. Ken tried to catch it, but a little boy got it first. The boy smiled so brightly that we both laughed. It was not a perfect game, but it was a great night.
cards.back: 上週末，我的同事 Ken 邀我去看棒球賽。我們的座位靠近外野，所以可以把球員看得很清楚。第三局時，一顆界外球朝我們飛來，大家都跳了起來。Ken 想接住它，但是一個小男孩先拿到了。男孩笑得好燦爛，我們兩個都笑了。這不是一場完美的比賽，但卻是美好的夜晚。
cards.note: 重點：outfield 外野／foul ball 界外球／clearly 清楚地

questions.q: Who invited the writer to the game?
questions.explain: 第一句：my coworker Ken invited me（同事 Ken 邀請我）。

questions.q: What flew toward them in the third inning?
questions.explain: 文中：a foul ball flew toward us（一顆界外球朝我們飛來）。

questions.q: Who got the ball?
questions.explain: 文中：a little boy got it first（一個小男孩先拿到了）。

cards.front: Yesterday I played pickleball for the first time. My friend explained the rules before we started. The most important rule is the kitchen, the area next to the net. You cannot volley the ball when you stand there. At first, I made many faults because I forgot this rule. After an hour, I started to remember it, and we played our first doubles game. I lost, but I want to play again.
cards.back: 昨天我第一次打匹克球。開始前，朋友先解釋了規則。最重要的規則是廚房區，也就是球網旁邊的區域。站在那裡時不能截擊。一開始我因為忘了這條規則，犯了很多次違例。一個小時後，我開始記住了，我們打了第一場雙打。我輸了，但我還想再打。
cards.note: 重點：kitchen 廚房區／fault 違例／doubles 雙打

questions.q: What is the kitchen in pickleball?
options: The area next to the net
A place to eat after games
The back line of the court
questions.explain: 文中：the kitchen, the area next to the net（廚房區就是球網旁邊的區域）。

questions.q: Why did the writer make many faults at first?
options: The writer forgot the kitchen rule
questions.explain: 文中：I made many faults because I forgot this rule（因為忘了這條規則而違例很多次）。

questions.q: How did the writer feel at the end?
questions.explain: 最後一句：I lost, but I want to play again。

cards.front: Before every game, our pickleball group warms up for ten minutes. We stretch our legs and arms, and then we hit some easy shots. Our coach says a good warm-up helps us avoid injuries. We also bring plenty of water because we sweat a lot. Last month, one player skipped the warm-up and hurt a muscle. Now nobody forgets it.
cards.back: 每場比賽前，我們的匹克球小組都會熱身十分鐘。我們伸展腿和手臂，然後打一些簡單的球。教練說好的熱身能幫助我們避免受傷。我們也會帶很多水，因為會流很多汗。上個月，有一位球友跳過熱身，拉傷了肌肉。現在沒有人會忘記熱身。
cards.note: 重點：warm up 熱身／stretch 伸展／injury 受傷

questions.q: How long does the group warm up before every game?
questions.explain: 第一句：warms up for ten minutes（熱身十分鐘）。

questions.q: According to the coach, why is a warm-up useful?
questions.explain: 文中：a good warm-up helps us avoid injuries（好的熱身能避免受傷）。

questions.q: What happened to the player who skipped the warm-up?
questions.explain: 文中：skipped the warm-up and hurt a muscle（跳過熱身，拉傷肌肉）。

cards.front: I wanted to see a baseball game with my sister, so we went to the stadium ticket office. I asked the clerk, "Do you have two seats together?" She said the cheap seats were sold out, but there were two seats behind home plate. The price was higher than I expected, but we decided to buy them. She gave us a receipt, and we walked into the stadium feeling excited.
cards.back: 我想和姊姊一起看棒球賽，所以我們去了球場售票處。我問售票員：「你們有兩個連在一起的座位嗎？」她說便宜的座位賣完了，但本壘板後方還有兩個位子。價錢比我預期的高，但我們決定買下來。她給了我們收據，我們興奮地走進球場。
cards.note: 重點：sold out 售完／behind home plate 本壘板後方／expect 預期

questions.q: Who did the writer want to see the game with?
questions.explain: 第一句：with my sister（和姊姊）。

questions.q: What did the clerk say about the cheap seats?
questions.explain: 文中：the cheap seats were sold out（便宜的座位賣完了）。

questions.q: How was the price compared with what the writer expected?
questions.explain: 文中：The price was higher than I expected（價格比預期的高）。

cards.front: Our club joined a pickleball tournament last Sunday. In the first round, our opponents were much taller than us, and they served very hard. We kept the ball low and tried to hit it near their baseline. In the last point, our ball landed out of bounds, so we lost the match. We did not win the trophy, but we learned a lot. Next time, we will practice our serve more.
cards.back: 上週日，我們的社團參加了匹克球比賽。第一輪時，對手比我們高很多，而且發球很用力。我們把球打得低一點，並試著打到他們的底線附近。最後一分，我們的球出界了，所以輸掉比賽。我們沒有拿到獎盃，但學到了很多。下次我們會多練習發球。
cards.note: 重點：opponent 對手／baseline 底線／out of bounds 出界

questions.q: What was true about the opponents in the first round?
options: They were much taller than the writer's team
questions.explain: 文中：our opponents were much taller than us（對手比我們高很多）。

questions.q: How did the team lose the match?
options: Their ball landed out of bounds on the last point
questions.explain: 文中：In the last point, our ball landed out of bounds, so we lost the match。

questions.q: What will the team do next time?
questions.explain: 最後一句：we will practice our serve more（下次多練發球）。

cards.front: In Taiwan, going to a baseball game is a lot of fun, even if you don't know the rules. Fans sing a special song for each player. When the pitcher throws a fastball, the whole stadium waits quietly. Then, after a strikeout, everyone shouts together. I think the best part is the food, because you can eat snacks while you cheer for your team.
cards.back: 在台灣，去看棒球賽非常有趣，即使你不懂規則也一樣。球迷會為每位球員唱專屬的歌。投手投出速球時，整個球場安靜地等待。然後，三振之後，大家一起大喊。我覺得最棒的部分是食物，因為你可以一邊吃零食，一邊為你的球隊加油。
cards.note: 重點：fastball 速球／strikeout 三振／cheer 加油

questions.q: What do fans do for each player?
questions.explain: 文中：Fans sing a special song for each player（球迷為每位球員唱專屬的歌）。

questions.q: What does the whole stadium do when the pitcher throws a fastball?
questions.explain: 文中：the whole stadium waits quietly（整個球場安靜等待）。

questions.q: What does the writer think is the best part?
questions.explain: 最後一句：I think the best part is the food。

cards.front: The man who sits next to me is my new supervisor.
cards.back: 坐在我旁邊的男士是我的新主管。
cards.note: who：關係代名詞，修飾「人」，在子句中當主詞。

cards.front: This is the hotel where we stayed last year.
cards.back: 這是我們去年住的飯店。
cards.note: where：修飾地點，後面接完整子句（主詞 + 動詞）。

cards.front: I lost the book which I borrowed from the library.
cards.back: 我弄丟了向圖書館借的書。
cards.note: which：修飾「物」。which 當受詞時可以省略。

cards.front: The restaurant that we went to was crowded.
cards.note: that 可代替 who / which；介系詞（went to）留在動詞後面。

cards.front: She is the player whose serve is the fastest.
cards.note: whose：表示所有關係（她的發球），後面接名詞。

cards.front: The tickets I bought online were cheaper.
cards.back: 我在網路上買的票比較便宜。
cards.note: 受詞關係代名詞可以省略：The tickets (that) I bought online。

cards.front: My manager, who has worked here for ten years, is retiring.
cards.back: 我的主管在這裡工作十年了，他要退休了。
cards.note: 逗號隔開的補充說明：要用 who / which，不能用 that。

cards.front: I know a café where you can study quietly.
cards.back: 我知道一家可以安靜念書的咖啡店。
cards.note: where 引導的子句可以直接說明地點的特色。

cards.front: Could you tell me where the baggage claim is?
cards.back: 可以告訴我行李提領處在哪裡嗎？
cards.note: 間接問句用肯定句語序：where the baggage claim is（不是 where is the baggage claim）。

cards.front: I wonder how much the tickets will cost.
cards.back: 我想知道門票要多少錢。
cards.note: I wonder / I don't know / Do you know + 疑問詞 + 主詞 + 動詞（肯定句語序）。

cards.front: The meeting was postponed until next Monday.
cards.note: 被動語態：be + 過去分詞（was postponed）。重點是事情，不強調誰做的。

cards.front: The stadium was built in 1990 and has been renovated twice.
cards.back: 這座球場建於一九九〇年，之後整修過兩次。
cards.note: 現在完成式被動：has / have been + 過去分詞。

cards.front: By the time we got to the airport, the check-in desk had already closed.
cards.back: 等我們到機場時，報到櫃檯已經關了。
cards.note: 過去完成式 had + 過去分詞：在過去某個時間點之前就已經完成的事。

cards.front: The game had already started when we found our seats.
cards.back: 我們找到座位時，比賽已經開始了。
cards.note: 兩件過去的事，先發生的用過去完成式（had started），後發生的用過去式（found）。

cards.front: I wish I had booked the tickets earlier.
cards.note: wish + 過去完成式：對過去的遺憾。對現在的願望用 wish + 過去式（I wish I had more time）。

cards.front: If I had more vacation days, I would travel more.
cards.back: 如果我有更多假期，我會多去旅行。
cards.note: 第二類條件句（與現在事實相反）：if + 過去式，would + 原形。

cards.front: Not only did we win, but we also scored a record number of runs.
cards.back: 我們不只贏了，還得到了破紀錄的分數。
cards.note: Not only 放句首時要倒裝：did we win（助動詞 + 主詞）。
We need to meet the deadline on Friday.
Let's schedule a meeting for next week.
I'm having lunch with a colleague.
She presented a proposal for the new project.
The project is over budget.
Will you attend the conference next month?
We negotiated a better price with the supplier.
Who is responsible for this task?
Customer service is our top priority.
Thanks for your feedback on my report.
What's on the agenda for today's meeting?
I'll follow up with you by email tomorrow.
Could you take the minutes during the meeting?
Can we reschedule the meeting for Thursday?

I forgot to open the attachment in your email.
Please forward the email to the whole team.
I'll reply to your message this afternoon.

Our sales target for this quarter is high.

Do you have any experience in marketing?
Good communication is an important skill at work.

Please send the invoice by the end of the month.

cards.front: On Monday morning, my team had a meeting to discuss a new project. Our manager explained the goals and asked everyone to share ideas. We agreed on a deadline of three weeks. After the meeting, I wrote down my tasks and sent an email to my colleagues. I felt a little nervous, but I was excited to start.
cards.back: 週一早上，我的團隊開會討論一個新專案。主管說明了目標，並請大家分享想法。我們同意以三週為期限。會後，我寫下自己的工作項目，並寄信給同事。我有一點緊張，但也很期待開始。
cards.note: 重點：goal 目標／deadline 期限／task 工作項目

questions.q: What was the meeting about?
questions.explain: 第一句：to discuss a new project（討論新專案）。

questions.q: How long did the team have to finish?
questions.explain: 文中：a deadline of three weeks（三週的期限）。

questions.q: How did the writer feel at the end?
questions.explain: 最後一句：I felt a little nervous, but I was excited to start。

cards.front: Last week I finished a report for a client. Before sending it, I asked my colleague to read it and give me some feedback. She said the data was clear, but the summary was too long. I shortened it and added a chart. The client liked the new version and thanked us for the quick response.
cards.back: 上週我完成了一份給客戶的報告。寄出前，我請同事先看過並給我一些意見。她說資料很清楚，但摘要太長。我把它縮短，又加了一張圖表。客戶很喜歡新版本，並感謝我們快速回覆。
cards.note: 重點：client 客戶／feedback 回饋／summary 摘要

questions.q: Who read the report before it was sent?
questions.explain: 文中：I asked my colleague to read it（請同事先看）。

questions.q: What was wrong with the report, according to the colleague?
questions.explain: 文中：the data was clear, but the summary was too long（資料很清楚，但摘要太長）。

questions.q: What did the writer add to the report?
questions.explain: 文中：I shortened it and added a chart（縮短後加了圖表）。

cards.front: Some companies let employees work from home a few days a week. People who work at home save time because they don't have to commute. However, it can be hard to separate work from personal life. To stay productive, many people set a fixed schedule and take short breaks. Others miss talking face to face with their coworkers.
cards.back: 有些公司讓員工每週在家工作幾天。在家工作的人可以省下通勤時間。不過，要把工作和私人生活分開可能不容易。為了保持效率，許多人會訂定固定的作息並短暫休息。也有人懷念和同事面對面聊天。
cards.note: 重點：commute 通勤／productive 有效率的／face to face 面對面

questions.q: Why do people who work at home save time?
questions.explain: 文中：they don't have to commute（不用通勤）。

questions.q: What can be hard when working at home?
questions.explain: 文中：it can be hard to separate work from personal life（很難把工作和私生活分開）。

questions.q: What do some people miss?
options: Talking face to face with coworkers
questions.explain: 最後一句：miss talking face to face with their coworkers（懷念和同事面對面聊天）。

cards.front: This morning I received an email from a new client. She asked for a price list, so I opened the attachment and checked the numbers. Then I forwarded the email to my manager because I was not sure about one price. He replied in ten minutes and fixed the mistake. I thanked him and sent the final list to the client before lunch.
cards.back: 今天早上我收到一位新客戶的電子郵件。她要一份價目表，所以我打開附件，檢查了數字。接著我把信轉寄給我的主管，因為我不確定其中一個價格。他十分鐘內就回信，並改正了錯誤。我向他道謝，並在午餐前把最後的價目表寄給客戶。
cards.note: 重點：attachment 附件／forward 轉寄／reply 回覆

questions.q: What did the new client ask for?
questions.explain: 文中：She asked for a price list（她要價目表）。

questions.q: Why did the writer forward the email to the manager?
options: The writer was not sure about one price
The writer wanted a day off
questions.explain: 文中：because I was not sure about one price（不確定其中一個價格）。

questions.q: When did the writer send the final list to the client?
questions.explain: 最後一句：before lunch（午餐前）。

cards.front: Last week I had a job interview at a travel company. I updated my CV and practiced answering questions the night before. At the interview, the manager asked about my experience and my skills. I was nervous, but I spoke slowly and smiled. At the end, she said they would call me in three days. I am still waiting, but I feel proud of myself.
cards.back: 上週我去一家旅行社面試。前一晚我更新了履歷，並練習回答問題。面試時，主管問了我的經驗和技能。我很緊張，但我說得很慢，也面帶微笑。最後她說三天後會打電話給我。我還在等，但我為自己感到驕傲。
cards.note: 重點：interview 面試／CV 履歷／experience 經驗

questions.q: What kind of company was the interview at?
questions.explain: 第一句：a job interview at a travel company。

questions.q: What did the writer do the night before?
options: Updated the CV and practiced answering questions
questions.explain: 文中：I updated my CV and practiced answering questions the night before。

questions.q: What is the writer doing now?
questions.explain: 文中：I am still waiting（我還在等）。

cards.front: This month my workload is very heavy. Two projects have the same deadline, so I worked overtime almost every night. My supervisor noticed that I looked tired, and she asked me to make a list of my tasks. We decided to move one task to another colleague. It was a good solution, and now I can go home on time again.
cards.back: 這個月我的工作量很大。兩個專案的截止日期是同一天，所以我幾乎每天晚上都加班。我的主管注意到我看起來很累，請我列出所有工作項目。我們決定把其中一項交給另一位同事。這是個好辦法，現在我又能準時回家了。
cards.note: 重點：workload 工作量／overtime 加班／task 工作項目

questions.q: Why did the writer work overtime?
options: Two projects had the same deadline
questions.explain: 文中：Two projects have the same deadline（兩個專案同一天截止）。

questions.q: What did the supervisor ask the writer to do?
questions.explain: 文中：she asked me to make a list of my tasks（請我列出工作項目）。

questions.q: What was the solution?
options: Move one task to another colleague
questions.explain: 文中：We decided to move one task to another colleague。

cards.front: Our client wanted to meet on Tuesday, but my manager was sick. I wrote an email to ask if we could reschedule the meeting for Thursday. The client replied quickly and said Thursday was fine. I changed the schedule, sent a new invitation, and prepared the presentation again. Everything went well, and the client liked our plan.
cards.back: 我們的客戶想在週二開會，但我的主管生病了。我寫了一封信，問能不能把會議改到週四。客戶很快回覆，說週四可以。我更改了行程，寄出新的邀請，並重新準備簡報。一切都很順利，客戶也喜歡我們的計畫。
cards.note: 重點：reschedule 改期／invitation 邀請／presentation 簡報

questions.q: Why did the writer need to reschedule the meeting?
questions.explain: 文中：my manager was sick（主管生病了）。

questions.q: What day was the new meeting?
questions.explain: 文中：reschedule the meeting for Thursday（改到週四）。

questions.q: How did the client respond?
options: Replied quickly and said Thursday was fine
questions.explain: 文中：The client replied quickly and said Thursday was fine。

cards.front: After two years at my company, I decided to ask for a raise. First, I wrote down what I achieved: I delivered three projects on time and helped two new employees. Then I made an appointment with my supervisor. She listened carefully and said she would talk to her boss. A week later, I got a small raise and a better position.
cards.back: 在公司工作兩年後，我決定要求加薪。首先，我寫下自己的成果：我準時交付了三個專案，還幫助了兩位新進員工。接著我和主管約了時間。她仔細聽完，說會和她的上司談談。一週後，我得到小幅加薪和更好的職位。
cards.note: 重點：raise 加薪／achieve 達成／deliver 交付

questions.q: How long had the writer worked at the company?
questions.explain: 第一句：After two years at my company。

questions.q: What did the writer do first?
options: Wrote down what the writer achieved
questions.explain: 文中：First, I wrote down what I achieved（先寫下自己的成果）。

questions.q: What happened a week later?
options: The writer got a small raise and a better position
questions.explain: 最後一句：A week later, I got a small raise and a better position。

cards.front: Our team will launch a new app next month. Every week, we hold a short meeting to check our progress. The designers show their work, and the engineers explain what they finished. If someone has a problem, we collaborate to find a solution. Because we communicate clearly, we have not missed a single target so far.
cards.back: 我們的團隊下個月要推出一個新的應用程式。每週我們都開一場簡短的會議來確認進度。設計師展示他們的作品，工程師說明完成了什麼。如果有人遇到問題，我們會合作找出解決辦法。因為我們溝通清楚，到目前為止沒有錯過任何一個目標。
cards.note: 重點：launch 推出／progress 進度／collaborate 合作

questions.q: When will the team launch the app?
questions.explain: 第一句：will launch a new app next month。

questions.q: What do the engineers do in the weekly meeting?
questions.explain: 文中：the engineers explain what they finished（工程師說明完成了什麼）；設計師才是展示作品。

questions.q: Why has the team not missed a single target so far?
options: They have a very small project
questions.explain: 最後一句：Because we communicate clearly（因為溝通清楚）。

cards.front: Yesterday I joined a conference call with colleagues in three countries. The meeting started late because someone's internet was slow. Our manager kept the agenda brief, so we finished in thirty minutes. Before we ended the call, someone took the minutes and promised to send them by email. I like short meetings like this because I can finish my other work.
cards.back: 昨天我參加了一場有三個國家同事的電話會議。會議晚開始，因為有人的網路很慢。我們的主管把議程控制得很精簡，所以三十分鐘就結束了。結束通話前，有人做了會議記錄，並答應用電子郵件寄出。我喜歡這種短會議，因為我能完成其他工作。
cards.note: 重點：conference call 電話會議／agenda 議程／minutes 會議記錄

questions.q: Why did the meeting start late?
questions.explain: 文中：because someone's internet was slow（有人的網路很慢）。

questions.q: How long was the call?
questions.explain: 文中：we finished in thirty minutes（三十分鐘就結束）。

questions.q: Why does the writer like short meetings?
options: The writer can finish other work
questions.explain: 最後一句：because I can finish my other work。

cards.front: He said that he was tired.
cards.note: 轉述時時態往後退一格：am / is → was。

cards.front: She told me that she would send the file.
cards.note: will → would；tell + 人 + that。

cards.front: They said they had already left the hotel.
cards.note: 過去式／現在完成式 → had + 過去分詞。

cards.front: He asked if I wanted some coffee.
cards.note: 轉述是非問句：if / whether + 肯定句語序。

cards.front: She asked where the meeting room was.
cards.note: 轉述疑問句：where + 主詞 + 動詞（不倒裝）。

cards.front: The coach told us to warm up first.
cards.note: tell + 人 + to V：轉述命令或要求。

cards.front: My boss asked me not to be late.
cards.note: 否定的要求：not to V（not 放在 to 前面）。

cards.front: He promised to call back in an hour.
cards.note: promise + to V：轉述承諾。
